title: LLM in a flash: Efficient Large Language Model Inference with Limited Memory
technique: Flash-resident weights loaded on demand using FFN activation sparsity: windowing (reuse recently activated neurons), row-column bundling for larger contiguous reads, DRAM management; cost model of flash I/O

optimized_metrics.evidence: Our primary metric for evaluating various flash loading strategies is latency, dissected into three distinct components: the I/O cost of loading from flash, the overhead of managing memory with newly loaded data, and the compute cost for inference operations.
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: Figure 1: Average inference latency for a single token

optimized_metrics.evidence: guiding us to optimize in two critical areas: reducing the volume of data transferred from flash and reading data in larger, more contiguous chunks
This paper tackles the challenge of efficiently running LLMs that exceed the available DRAM capacity by storing the model parameters in flash memory, but bringing them on demand to DRAM.

headline_claim.text: These methods collectively enable running models up to twice the size of the available DRAM, with up to 4x and 20x increase in inference speed compared to naive loading approaches in CPU and GPU, respectively.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 1, Tables 2-3: average per-token inference latency (ms) split into compute / flash load / memory management
I/O transferred volume per token (e.g. fraction of model loaded) in Fig 5-8, Table 2
Table 4: zero-shot accuracy of predictors; MMLU
